biomarkers.name: RB1 mutation (germline or somatic)
biomarkers.prevalence: >95% overall; biallelic RB1 inactivation is the defining event in the great majority of tumours
biomarkers.clinical_use: Bilateral / familial disease is usually due to germline RB1 alteration; germline RB1 is identified in ~90–95% of bilateral cases. Cascade family testing is critical — germline carriers have lifetime risk of second cancers (osteosarcoma, soft-tissue sarcoma, melanoma, brain tumours). Chemoreduction, focal therapy, or enucleation depending on stage

biomarkers.name: MYCN amplification
biomarkers.clinical_use: Rare RB1-wildtype MYCN-amplified retinoblastoma subset — typically unilateral and clinically aggressive

biomarkers.name: Chromosome 6p gain, 1q gain, 16q loss
biomarkers.clinical_use: Secondary genomic events recurrent in retinoblastoma; associated with tumour progression/adverse pathologic features

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small round blue cell embryonal tumour of retina with Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (true rosettes with central lumen) and Homer-Wright rosettes (pseudorosettes)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: AJCC / International Retinoblastoma Classification for treatment decisions

tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Retinal architecture; necrosis common with calcification

cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Neuroectoderm — retina from diencephalic outpouching (optic vesicle)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Embryonal / photoreceptor-directed differentiation with Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (true rosettes with central lumen mimicking photoreceptor outer segment) and Homer-Wright rosettes (pseudorosettes)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Biallelic RB1 loss is the defining genomic event in most tumours — pRB loss releases E2F transcription factors and disrupts cell cycle control; cone precursors are particularly vulnerable because of their unique cell cycle regulation
